To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
various patterns in nucleosomal sequences are related to the packing and regulatory roles of chromatin.
various distinct NPS patterns in the nucleosomal DNA can have different functions: packing function to the WW/SS pattern and regulatory function to the RR/ YY and “anti” NPS patterns.
the NPS patterns are related to two main functions of chromatin, namely packing and gene expression regulatory.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the analysis of nucleosomal DNA sequences in the context of their role in the chromatin structure, chromatin function and regulation of gene expression.
the analysis of nucleosome positioning patterns in the genomes of different species.
understanding of the nucleosome positioning and its role in the chromatin structure and function.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the NPS pattern in yeast is more similar to the NPS in human apoptotic cells than to the NPS patterns observed in mouse brain or normal human cells.
nucleosomes with WW/SS patterns are involved in the chromatin packing function, while RR/YY and “antipatterns” are involved in the regulation function of chromatin.
the WW/SS and the RR/YY patterns are two different modes of the same function of chromatin: packing and regulating gene expression.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the nucleosomal DNA sequence patterns are highly variable between organisms and cell types, and the patterns are not random.
Nucleosome positioning sequence ( NPS) patterns are a key to understanding the chromatin organization and its functions.

NPS patterns can be classified into two groups: packing and regulatory, with the former group being related to the packing of DNA into nucleosome particles and the latter group related to gene expression regulation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the NPS patterns are highly correlated in the same cell types of different species.
the nucleosomal DNA sequence elements can be used to predict nucleosome positioning and to identify regulatory and packaging functions of chromatin.
different patterns in nucleosomal DNAs are related to two main functions: packing of chromatin and gene regulatory processes.
